docs.title: Agents — JARVIS + specialists (ZealBot)
docs.text: /jarvis assigns tasks in natural language. JARVIS (orchestrator) understands, routes to the right specialist and stays responsible for the result. Specialists never call each other: only JARVIS → specialist (same principle as the Commander: brain → muscles).

docs.title: The agents
docs.text:
Agent Role Example tasks ⚡ JARVIS Orchestrator + generalist anything; routes when needed 🛡️ Sentinel Moderation and safety anti-raid plans, automod thresholds, ban procedures 🎫 Steward Tickets and support canned replies, intake forms 🎵 Maestro Music and voice queues, music command setup 💰 Banker Economy and levels balances, rewards, XP tuning 📚 Lore Knowledge and code summaries, explanations, server memory 🔭 Scout Web and external services reading pages, using logged-in services

Usage: /jarvis task:<text> (JARVIS chooses) or /jarvis task:<text> agent:scout (forced). AI-less routing is keyword-based and always works; with an AI key (even free by default, see .env.example) specialists reason in steps (ReAct, max JARVIS_MAX_STEPS).

docs.title: Per-agent sandbox
docs.text:
Every run executes in an application sandbox (src/agents/sandbox.js):

  • capability-based: only manifest tools (say, note, fetchUrl, useService, askOwner) — no free require/fs/network;
  • jail directory: data/sandboxes/<agent>/ (gitignored);
  • timeout: JARVIS_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS (default 2 min);
  • audit: start/end/errors in the logger, never secrets in logs.

It's logical isolation, not a VM: it protects against errors and tool abuse, not hostile native code (plugins stay isolated via the pluginLoader).

docs.title: Goggles — the control-room (/agents.html)
docs.text:
Agents don't have a screen to truly share: the goggles are the live trace of every session (thoughts → actions → observations → result), visible live on the dashboard and fed by the shared store (bot and dashboard are separate processes).

From the control-room you can:

  • 👁️ enter the screen: open a session and watch the live stream (SSE);
  • 🎧 take over: dictate an instruction read at the next step;
  • ✅/⛔ approve or deny pending requests;
  • 🔑 see which services hold vault credentials (never the values).

On Discord, approvals also arrive as buttons (Approve/Deny) in the channel where you ran /jarvis.

docs.title: Vault — service logins
docs.text:
The owner stores credentials (tokens/API keys) and agents use the services without ever seeing the secrets:

  1. set VAULT_KEY in .env (min 16 chars, never commit it);
  2. store the credential (via code: vault.storeSecret(service, account, secret));
  3. the specialist (today only Scout) calls useService: an approval request starts (dashboard + Discord);
  4. once approved → the broker injects Authorization: Bearer <secret> into an https call and returns only the outcome (the secret is redacted if it reappears in the output).

Honest limits: Bearer-only over https, no internal hosts; no bypassing captchas/2FA/interactive logins — humans handle those. Every use is tracked (service, account, agent, session).

docs.text: How to drive the bot from code (commands, dashboard, MCP, CLI all go through here). Italian edition: API.it.md.

docs.title: Commander (src/modules/commander.js + packages/commander core)
docs.text:
Single orchestrator. Never require modules/registry directly (smoke [8/5] forbids it).

Method Signature What it does checkGate(commandName, guildId) (string, string?) {ok:true} or {ok:false, reason:'disabled'\|'isolated', featureId}. Resolves the command → feature first. canRun(guildId, featureId) (string?, string?) Same gate by feature id (for events/handlers). Fail-open. executeCommand(command, interaction, client, opts?) opts.timeoutMs (default 15000) Runs command.execute isolated with timeout; records errors (breaker). Never throws: {ok, timedOut?, error?}. guardEvent(file, event, args, client) — Wraps every listener: skips if the module can't run, records errors. Never throws. featureOfCommand/Event/Component (string) name → feature id (or null = always allowed). listModules() — Static descriptors (id, version, commands…). moduleHealth(guildId) — Per-guild state: enabled, isolated, errors, stats. setModuleEnabled(guildId, id, on) — Toggle (re-enable also clears breaker+errors). Throws on unknown id. reloadModule(guildId, id) — Revalidates syntax, reloads descriptor, clears errors+breaker. resetModule(guildId, id) — Clears errors+breaker. updateModuleConfig(guildId, mod, patch) — Dispatches a validated patch to the right module DB. Throws {status, message}. alertsPending() — Queued pain signals (Guardian). guardianSummary(guildId) — TS-core health scores (see below).

docs.title: Guardian (immune system)
docs.text:
• Score (passive): TS core packages/commander (Guardian.observe/summary): ok/fail/timeout per guild+feature → {features, critical, weak, ok}. No LLM in the hot path.
  • Pain (active): registry.recordError returns {tripped}; on trip a de-duplicated signal is queued (drainAlerts, 15-min window). src/jobs/guardianJob.js delivers to the guild log channel every 2 min; ≥3 isolated modules = fever alert (1/hour).
  • Skin: src/events/secretGuard.js deletes leaked tokens/keys + DM + modlog.
  • Read health anytime: commander.guardianSummary(gid), commander.alertsPending().

docs.title: Per-guild configuration
docs.text:
Two layers (same ones /config and the dashboard use):

  1. Module toggles — commander.setModuleEnabled(gid, id, on) (persistent via moduleState).
  2. Module settings — commander.updateModuleConfig(gid, mod, patch) for general, welcome, logging, levels, automod, autorole, starboard, confessioni, tickets, tempvoice, ai (validated upstream; see dashboard MODULE_FIELDS).
  3. Runtime env overrides — database/settings.js (setOverride/getOverride/effectiveEnv, strict whitelist). Read via effectiveEnv(), never process.env directly for tunable keys.

docs.title: Extending with a new module
docs.text:
1. Descriptor src/modules/<id>.js via defineModule({id, title, commands, version…}) (validated, semver required).
  2. Slash commands in src/commands/<area>/ (auto-loaded recursively).
  3. Listeners in src/events/ (one file per listener; shared Discord events are an allowed pattern, never bypass the gate — use commander.canRun).
  4. State in src/database/<name>.js over jsonDb (additive migrations in schema.js with __v stamp).
  5. Register the feature id in commander.featureOf* maps only via the descriptor (no hardcoded lists elsewhere).
  6. Docs: command appears in docs/COMMANDS.md via node scripts/gen-docs.js; add a smoke section with qatest keys + cleanup.

docs.title: Bot architecture
docs.text: Map derived from reading the code (entry point src/index.js, events, database, dashboard, jobs). File names and behaviors match what is implemented, not future intentions.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ZealBot — multi-server Discord bot based on discord.js v14, CommonJS, single Node process (node src/index.js). Slash commands organized by category-folder, persistent state in JSON (with optional SQLite backend), web dashboard in a separate process, periodic jobs started on the ready event. Variable details in CONFIG.md, commands in COMMANDS.md (generated with node scripts/gen-docs.js).

docs.title: Folder structure
docs.text: Path Role src/index.js Entry point: client, command/event loading, login, conditional dashboard startup src/commands/<category>/*.js Slash commands (data + execute + cooldown); the category is the folder name (ai, economy, fun, levels, moderation, music, tickets, utility) src/events/*.js One file per listener (name + execute + once?); see multi-listener pattern below src/handlers/ ticketHandler.js, reactionRoleHandler.js: handle selects/modals/buttons before commands src/database/ store.js + jsonDb.js (infrastructure) + ~25 domain modules (economy.js, levels.js, …) + respective <name>.json + moduleState.js (per-guild feature on/off) src/modules/ Feature controllers: registry.js + one file per part (tickets.js, levels.js, … with mapped commands/db/events); command/event gates, dashboard toggles, health and per-module isolated errors src/dashboard/ index.js (standalone process), server.js, auth.js, api.js, guilds.js (client/REST source), presence.js (roster), discordRest.js (REST reads), public/: web app Express separate from the bot src/jobs/ ticketAutoclose.js, backup.js, selfImprove.js: timers started by events/ready.js, never started elsewhere src/utils/ logger.js, i18n.js, ai.js/aiProviders.js, player.js, codebase.js, helpers.js, transcript.js, … src/locales/ it.js, en.js for utils/i18n.js scripts/smoke-test.js QA (npm test): commands, events, DB roundtrips on qatest keys, require-safe scripts/gen-docs.js Generates docs/COMMANDS.md with no network nor bot deploy-commands.js Registers slash commands on Discord (test guild or global)

docs.title: Boot (src/index.js)
docs.text:
1. dotenv, require DISCORD_TOKEN (exit 1 if missing).
  2. Client with 8 intents (Guilds, GuildMessages, MessageContent, GuildMembers, GuildModeration, GuildMessageReactions, GuildVoiceStates, GuildInvites) and partials (Message, Channel, GuildMember, Reaction).
  3. client.commands / client.cooldowns (Collection), client.spamMap (in-memory anti-spam Map).
  4. loadCommands(src/commands) recursive: assigns command.category = <folder name>, skips files without data/execute with a warning, reports duplicate slash names without silently overwriting (last one wins in the Collection, with console.warn). A failed require skips only that file, never the whole bot.
  5. Event registration: one client.on/client.once per file, with validation (name string + execute function); invalid files skipped with warning.
  6. unhandledRejection/uncaughtException handlers: console + structured logger, never crash.
  7. client.login(DISCORD_TOKEN); the bot also writes the guild roster (presence) for the standalone dashboard. Never dashboard logic here.

docs.title: Interaction → command flow (src/events/interactionCreate.js)
docs.text:
Exact pipeline order for every InteractionCreate:

  1. ticketHandler.handle(interaction) — if consumed (selects, modals, ticket buttons), stop.
  2. reactionRoleHandler.handle(interaction) — if consumed (select rr_select), stop. Both with dedicated ephemeral error reply.
  3. nuke_* buttons — nuke_cancel aborts; nuke_confirm requires ManageChannels permission, clones the channel, deletes the original and confirms (reply via webhook because the original channel no longer exists).
  4. Only isChatInputCommand() continues; command looked up in client.commands by interaction.commandName.
  5. Controller gate (src/modules/registry): if the command's feature is off for the guild, stop with ephemeral reply (DMs always allowed). execute errors are recorded per feature (dashboard).
  6. Custom permissions (database/customPerms, PeakBot-style) — per-command roles per guild, with Administrator bypass. It runs before the cooldown on purpose: rejected users don't consume wait time.
  7. Cooldown per command+user (command.cooldown || 3 seconds), with ephemeral relative-timestamp wait message.
  8. command.execute(interaction, client) + logCommand(...) for analytics. On error: structured log, best-effort embed in the guild's logChannelId (database/guildConfig), cooldown refund (timestamps.delete) so an error never costs wait time, generic ephemeral reply.

docs.title: Multi-listener pattern (events)
docs.text:
index.js registers one listener per file, so multiple files on the same Discord event are multiple active listeners — a deliberate pattern only for these events (verified by the smoke test, disjoint bodies):

  • guildMemberAdd — welcome (guildMemberAdd.js), autorole (autorole.js), anti-raid (antiRaid.js), joins analytics (analyticsMembers.js), invites (inviteTracker.js).
  • messageCreate — XP/automod (messageCreate.js), autoresponder (autoResponder.js, read-only + reply), analytics counting (analyticsMessages.js).
  • voiceStateUpdate — temporary voice rooms (tempVoice.js), voice XP (voiceXp.js).

Any other duplicated event across two files is an error (the smoke test fails). Other notable single listeners: aiMention.js, aiModeration.js, auditLog.js, customCommands.js, starboard.js, snipe via utils/snipeCache.js, ready.js.

docs.title: Persistence (src/database/store.js + jsonDb.js)
docs.text:
• store.js — synchronous collection(name) API with get/set/update/delete/all. Backend from env on every operation (tests switch env at runtime):
  • DB_BACKEND=json (default): src/database/<name>.json files, atomic read-modify-write via tmp+rename; corrupt files copied to <file>.corrupt-<timestamp> instead of losing them.
  • DB_BACKEND=sqlite: node:sqlite on DB_SQLITE_PATH (default ./data/bot.db), kv(collection, key, value) table with JSON values, journal_mode=WAL, transactions on multi-row replace; if the driver is missing or open fails, fallback to json with warning (never crash, never data loss).
  • Postgres future, not active: only schema in src/database/postgres-schema.sql; would require a separate async API.
  • jsonDb.js — load/save/dbFile compat layer over store.js, so the ~25 domain modules (economy, levels, warnings, guildConfig, tickets, cases, shop, lotteria, rep, sfide, confessioni, reactionRoles, autoresponder, invites, tempvoice, stanze, levelRewards, analytics, customPerms, customCommands, aiConfig, starboard, …) work unchanged on both backends.

docs.title: Separate-process dashboard (src/dashboard/)
docs.text:
• Started with npm run dashboard (src/dashboard/index.js, requires DASHBOARD_PORT); express is required lazy inside startDashboard() so the smoke test passes even without express installed.
  • Reads the same bot DB store (no syncing) + presence roster written by the bot; live Discord details via REST with the Bot token.
  • server.js: 256kb JSON limit, public/ static, auth routes, /api protected by auth.requireAuth, landing with inline fallback if public/index.html is missing, JSON 404, never-crashing error handler.
  • auth.js: Discord OAuth2 (redirect <BASE_URL>/callback, scopes identify+guilds) with SESSION_SECRET, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, BASE_URL.
  • api.js: per-guild API restricted to the admins of shared servers.

docs.title: Jobs (src/jobs/, started by src/events/ready.js)
docs.text:
Job Schedule What it does ticketAutoclose every 15 min Closes tickets idle beyond autoCloseDays (setAutoClose, 0 = off, max 90) backup nightly at 03:00 local Copies src/database/*.json (+ sqlite if present) into backups/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm/, 7-day retention, backups/last.json journal; never crash selfImprove nightly at SELF_IMPROVE_TIME Active only with SELF_IMPROVE=1 (default off); re-reads the code and proposes one patch, never auto-commits, SELF_IMPROVE_DRY_RUN=1 for report-only

All use unref'd intervals so they never keep the process alive alone, and every start is wrapped in try/catch in ready.js.

docs.title: Command deploy and i18n
docs.text:
• deploy-commands.js — scans src/commands (one level), pushes data.toJSON() via REST: to the test guild if GUILD_ID is set, otherwise global (up to ~1h propagation).
  • utils/i18n.js + locales/it.js/en.js — per-guild localized reply texts (getLang/t); slash names and descriptions stay in Italian.
  • Music (utils/player.js, /musica command) — discord-player with extractor; voice-dependency errors mapped to Italian messages, never crash.

docs.title: Configuration (environment variables)
docs.text:
Every env read by the code (grep process.env in src/, deploy-commands.js) plus .env.example. Copy .env.example to .env and fill in at least the required ones. Never commit .env.

Per-server configuration (language, channels, welcome, automod, tickets, levels, AI, permissions) happens exclusively from the web dashboard (<BASE_URL>/app.html, Generale, Moderazione, Livelli, Ticket e Vocali, AI ed Extra, Permessi sections). This file only describes the process environment variables.

Variable Required Default Used in Notes DISCORD_TOKEN yes — src/index.js, deploy-commands.js Bot token. Without it, the bot exits with an error. CLIENT_ID yes (for command deploy and dashboard) — deploy-commands.js, src/dashboard/auth.js Application ID. deploy-commands.js uses it with no fallback. GUILD_ID no — (global deploy) deploy-commands.js If set, registers commands only on the test server (fast); otherwise global (up to ~1h). AI_PROVIDER no auto src/utils/aiProviders.js auto picks from present keys; values: openai, anthropic, gemini, groq, openrouter, mistral, deepseek, xai, together, cerebras, ollama, fireworks, novita, huggingface, nvidia, kimi, pollinations (+ aliases claude, google, grok, hf); unknown value + AI_API_URL = custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint. OPENAI_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model gpt-4o-mini. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model claude-3-5-haiku-20241022. GEMINI_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model gemini-2.0-flash. GROQ_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model llama-3.3-70b-versatile. OPENROUTER_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model openai/gpt-4o-mini. MISTRAL_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model mistral-small-latest. DEEPSEEK_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model deepseek-chat. XAI_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model grok-3-mini. TOGETHER_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo. CEREBRAS_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model llama3.1-8b (very fast). Multiple comma-separated keys = Hermes-style pool (sk-a,sk-b: rotation + key failover). FIREWORKS_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6. NOVITA_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 (200+ models via AI_MODEL). HF_TOKEN no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Hugging Face Inference Providers, default deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2. NVIDIA_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Default model nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b. KIMI_API_KEY no (one is enough) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Moonshot, default kimi-for-coding. AI_MODEL no provider default model src/utils/aiProviders.js Accepts Hermes-style provider:model (e.g. groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile, wins over AI_PROVIDER). Endpoint override via <PREFIX>_BASE_URL (e.g. GROQ_BASE_URL). AI_FALLBACKS no — (no failover) src/utils/aiProviders.js E.g. groq,openrouter: if the primary fails (rate, timeout, network, HTTP, key), tries in order. If all fail, the shown error is the primary's. OLLAMA_HOST no http://localhost:11434 src/utils/aiProviders.js With AI_PROVIDER=ollama: local AI (default llama3.1), zero cloud, no keys. AI_API_URL no https://text.pollinations.ai src/utils/aiProviders.js Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint; without keys the free Pollinations is used, no key required. AI_API_KEY no — src/utils/aiProviders.js Key for custom AI_API_URL. AI_DAILY_LIMIT no 500 src/utils/ai.js Daily AI call budget on a shared key (0 = unlimited). Past the limit the AI replies "Budget giornaliero esaurito" (daily budget exhausted). DB_BACKEND no json src/database/store.js json (src/database/*.json files) or sqlite (kv table via node:sqlite, Node 22+). Anything other than sqlite falls back to json. DB_SQLITE_PATH no ./data/bot.db src/database/store.js, src/jobs/backup.js Sqlite database path (directory created if missing, journal_mode=WAL). Included in backup if the file exists. If node:sqlite is missing: fallback to json with warning. LOG_LEVEL no info src/utils/logger.js debug, info, warn, error. JSON-lines logs on console + logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log. LOG_DIR no logs src/utils/logger.js Directory for daily log files. BACKUP_DIR no backups src/jobs/backup.js Nightly backup destination YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm/, 7-day retention, last.json journal. Not in .env.example (found via grep). SELF_IMPROVE no off src/jobs/selfImprove.js Only =1 enables nightly self-improvement. Never auto-commits: review with git diff. SELF_IMPROVE_TIME no 22:00 src/jobs/selfImprove.js Local execution time. SELF_IMPROVE_DRY_RUN no off src/jobs/selfImprove.js =1: report only, no patch applied. SELF_IMPROVE_GUILD_ID no — (log only) src/jobs/selfImprove.js Server receiving the nightly report. DASHBOARD_PORT no — (dashboard off) src/dashboard/index.js Required by npm run dashboard (separate process); without it, the dashboard doesn't start. SESSION_SECRET yes (if dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js Session secret, at least 32 random characters. CLIENT_SECRET yes (if dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js Discord app client secret (OAuth2). BASE_URL yes (if dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js, /help command Public URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000); must match the OAuth2 redirect <BASE_URL>/callback. Also used in the /help footer.

Notes:

  • AI keys are alternatives: one key is enough and the provider is picked automatically (AI_PROVIDER=auto); without keys it works free via Pollinations (default AI_API_URL).
  • Fixed 25s AI timeout in code (src/utils/aiProviders.js), not configurable via env.
  • Backups always at 03:00 local with 7-day retention: code constants (src/jobs/backup.js), not env.

docs.title: Bot message languages (i18n)
docs.text:
Reply texts go through src/core/i18n.js (i18next engine with fs-backend over src/locales/<lang>.json, inline fallback if the backend fails): t(guildId, key, vars) with per-key fallback to English, getGuildLanguage(guildId) reads language from guildConfig (change it with /language, admins only; /lingua points to the dashboard). Supported languages: en, it (fallback en). src/utils/i18n.js keeps the legacy t(key, lang, vars) API on the same JSONs for existing callers.

Current coverage: moderation, economy, tickets, levels commands; slash names and descriptions stay in Italian.

To add a language (e.g. es):

  1. Copy src/locales/en.json to src/locales/es.json and translate the values (missing keys automatically fall back to English).
  2. Add 'es' to SUPPORTED in src/core/i18n.js (and SUPPORTED_LANGS in src/utils/i18n.js for legacy callers).
  3. Use t(guildId, 'key', { vars }) in new texts instead of hardcoded strings; don't churn existing texts without reason.

docs.title: Hosting — ZealBot
docs.text:
Guide in English to run the bot anywhere. Fast path for everyone:

npm run setup   # detects the host, verifies the token live, writes .env
npm run deploy  # registers slash commands
npm start       # bot (+ dashboard with npm run dashboard)

Common requirements:

  • Node.js ≥ 22.12 (recommended Node 24; @discordjs/voice requires it)
  • Toolchain: npm for everything (bot + Express dashboard).
  • .env file created from .env.example with at least DISCORD_TOKEN and CLIENT_ID
  • Slash command deploy: npm run deploy (after every command add/change)
  • Start: npm start (= node src/index.js) · Test: npm test

docs.title: Host matrix (auto-detected by src/host/)
docs.text:
Host Disk Recommended storage Dashboard Notes Render ephemeral sqlite on Disk (/app/data) ✅ via $PORT Blueprint render.yaml Railway ephemeral sqlite on Volume ✅ via $PORT railway.toml (root Dockerfile) Fly.io ephemeral sqlite on Volume (/app/data) ✅ port 3000 fly.toml (healthcheck /healthz: set the dashboard envs) Pterodactyl persistent sqlite ✅ panel port Generic NodeJS egg Docker ephemeral* sqlite on volume ✅ $PORT/3000 docker-compose.yml (*persistent with volume) VPS / local persistent sqlite (Node 22+) or json ✅ PM2 recommended Termux persistent json ✅ Development, not production Replit persistent json ✅ Always-on is paid

Data persistence: by default the bot uses JSON in src/database/*.json (DB_BACKEND=json). On hosts with an ephemeral filesystem (Railway/Render/Docker) use SQLite instead: DB_BACKEND=sqlite + DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db (requires Node ≥ 22, uses node:sqlite, zero extra dependencies), with the data/ folder on a persistent volume/disk.

docs.title: 1. Termux (Android)
docs.text:
pkg update && pkg install -y nodejs git
git clone <repo> zealbot && cd zealbot
npm ci
cp .env.example .env   # then fill it in with your editor
npm run deploy
npm start

Termux notes:

  • No systemd: to keep it alive use termux-wake-lock + a tmux session, or PM2 (npm i -g pm2 && pm2 start ecosystem.config.js && pm2 save). PM2 does not restart on phone reboot by itself: reopen Termux and run pm2 resurrect.
  • On Termux stay on DB_BACKEND=json (default) unless you have Node ≥ 22.
  • Logs go to logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log (LOG_LEVEL=info by default).

docs.title: 2. VPS (Debian/Ubuntu) — systemd or PM2
docs.text:
# Node 24 LTS (nodesource) + clone
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt install -y nodejs git
git clone <repo> /opt/zealbot && cd /opt/zealbot
npm ci --omit=dev
cp .env.example .env   # fill in DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, ...
npm run deploy

docs.title: Option A: systemd (recommended)
docs.text:
sudo cp zealbot.service /etc/systemd/system/zealbot.service
# adapt User/paths in the file if you don't use the "bot" user or /opt/zealbot
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now zealbot
systemctl status zealbot
journalctl -u zealbot -f   # live logs

The zealbot.service file uses WorkingDirectory=/opt/zealbot, EnvironmentFile=/opt/zealbot/.env and Restart=always.

docs.title: Option B: PM2
docs.text:
sudo npm i -g pm2
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js   # fork, 1 instance, logs in logs/pm2-*.log
pm2 save && pm2 startup         # automatic restart on boot
pm2 logs zealbot

One instance only, please (fork, never cluster): the bot uses file-based DB, two instances writing the same JSON/SQLite would corrupt the data.

docs.title: 3. Docker
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env   # fill in the values
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose logs -f

# With web dashboard (optional profile, requires DASHBOARD_* in .env):
docker compose --profile dashboard up -d --build
  • Dockerfile: node:24-slim base, npm ci --omit=dev, non-root node user, NODE_ENV=production, /app/data /app/logs /app/backups volumes.
  • docker-compose.yml: bot service (restart: unless-stopped, env_file: .env, ./data ./logs ./backups volumes); bot-dashboard service (only the dashboard profile) with published ${DASHBOARD_PORT:-3000} port.
  • Conditional healthcheck (see the Dockerfile comment): without DASHBOARD_PORT the bot exposes no HTTP, so the healthcheck immediately returns healthy (crashes are covered by restart: unless-stopped); with the dashboard on it hits GET /healthz (public endpoint with / fallback) via node -e ... fetch(...) with no need for curl in the image.
  • In containers set DB_BACKEND=sqlite + DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db (compose already defaults to it): the src/database/ JSON files are not mounted as a volume because they live alongside the .js modules (mounting the folder would hide the code from the container).
  • Music: the node:24-slim image does not include ffmpeg (needed by discord-player/@discordjs/voice). If you use music commands, add in the Dockerfile before USER node: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*.

docs.title: Prebuilt image (GHCR, no build)
docs.text:
Each vX.Y.Z tag publishes ghcr.io/zema-tech/zealbot-discord:latest (multi-arch amd64/arm64) via .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:

services:
  bot:
    image: ghcr.io/zema-tech/zealbot-discord:latest
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      DB_BACKEND: sqlite
      DB_SQLITE_PATH: /app/data/bot.db
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

docs.title: 4. Railway / Render
docs.text:
Fast path (Render): the repo includes render.yaml (Docker + /healthz healthcheck + 1GB disk): New → Blueprint, then fill in the secret envs (DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, BASE_URL). The blueprint already points SQLite at disk (DB_SQLITE_PATH=/app/data/bot.db).

Manual procedure (valid for both, ephemeral filesystem: persistent disk needed):

  1. Create the service from the repo (Build: npm ci, Start: node src/index.js).
  2. Set the Environment Variables from the panel (copy the keys from .env.example): DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, DB_BACKEND=sqlite, DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db, and possibly DASHBOARD_* (on Render also open the port with DASHBOARD_PORT).
  3. Mount a persistent disk on the data/ path (e.g. Railway Volume → mount /app/data; Render Disk on Docker runtime → mount /app/data, on native Node runtime → /opt/render/project/src/data): that's where bot.db, logs/ and backups/ live. Without a disk, every deploy starts from zero (economy, levels, tickets… lost).
  4. Run npm run deploy once (from local with the same env, or as a one-off job): registers slash commands on Discord.
  5. Render free: inactivity spin-down turns the bot off (the bot must stay always online) — you need an always-on instance or a paid plan.

docs.title: 5. Pterodactyl — egg note
docs.text:
No official egg: use a generic NodeJS egg (version 20):

  • Startup Command: node src/index.js
  • Install Script: npm ci (or npm ci --omit=dev)
  • Environment / Variables: DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID (+ DB_BACKEND, AI_*, DASHBOARD_* if needed) — or mount/upload an .env file in the server root.
  • Data stays on the Pterodactyl server disk (persistent across restarts); take regular backups of src/database/*.json (or data/bot.db if using SQLite) with the /backup command or from the panel.
  • The command deploy (node deploy-commands.js) runs once from console after setting the variables.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause and fix Unsupported URL Type "workspace:" on npm install Historical leftover: refresh the lock with npm install and retry (orphan workspaces were removed). DisallowedIntents / bot online but not responding Enable in the Developer Portal → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents: Server Members Intent and Message Content Intent (the bot uses GuildMembers + MessageContent, see src/index.js). GuildPresences is not needed. Missing or stale slash commands Run npm run deploy (needs CLIENT_ID; with GUILD_ID commands land instantly on the test server, otherwise allow up to ~1h for global propagation). TokenInvalid / TOKEN_INVALID Wrong or regenerated DISCORD_TOKEN: update .env (never commit it) and restart. Bot has no effect (roles, timeouts, channels) Permissions: invite the bot with bot + applications.commands scopes and adequate permissions (Manage roles/channels, Ban, Moderate members for timeouts, Connect/Speak for music). The bot role must sit above the roles it manages, otherwise Discord silently refuses. Dashboard: OAuth redirect failed BASE_URL must match the Redirect URI registered in the Discord portal (<BASE_URL>/callback, scopes identify+guilds); CLIENT_SECRET and SESSION_SECRET (≥32 chars) are also required. Port busy / dashboard won't open Change DASHBOARD_PORT in .env; verify the port is exposed (firewall/VPS, ports: in compose, open port on Render). Music won't start / voice errors ffmpeg and libsodium/opus dependencies are needed (on VPS: apt install ffmpeg; on Docker see §3). Without them, other commands work anyway. DB wiped after a redeploy Ephemeral filesystem without volume: switch to DB_BACKEND=sqlite with persistent data/ (§4). Locally, run /backup regularly (they land in backups/). Crash loop / constant restarts Read logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log (or journalctl/pm2 logs/docker compose logs): it's almost always an incomplete .env (missing DISCORD_TOKEN → immediate exit 1).

docs.title: MCP — bot remote control (Hermes Agent style)
docs.text:
Inspired by NousResearch/hermes-agent: same concepts (mcp_servers, tools.include/exclude, stdio + Streamable HTTP, mcp_<server>_<tool> prefix), adapted to the bot.

Direction What it does Config A. Server (AI → bot) Claude/ChatGPT operate the bot via POST /mcp /token crea, snippet in mcp/claude.example.json B. Client (bot → AI/tools) The bot uses external MCP servers as tools mcp/servers.json (from mcp/servers.example.json), /mcp command

docs.title: A. Server — bot remote control
docs.text: The bot exposes an MCP server (Streamable HTTP) on POST /mcp. Protocol (src/mcp/protocol.js) and Bearer auth (src/mcp/auth.js) are stable and untouchable: every token is valid for one server only and every tool enforces it.

docs.title: A.1. Create the token (once, from Discord)
docs.text:
As the server owner:

/token crea nome:claude-casa

Copy the shown token (it won't be recoverable) and the endpoint:

https://TUO-HOST/mcp

docs.title: A.2. Connect Claude
docs.text:
Claude Code (recommended):

claude mcp add --transport http zealbot https://TUO-HOST/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer dbt_..."

Claude Desktop: Settings → Connectors → Add with URL + header Authorization: Bearer dbt_.... The same snippet is ready in mcp/claude.example.json.

Other MCP clients: POST /mcp endpoint, 2025-06-18 protocol, initialize (replies with Mcp-Session-Id header, send it back), tools/list, tools/call. GET /mcp opens an SSE stream (needs a session), DELETE /mcp closes it.

Code layout: src/mcp/ — protocol.js (JSON-RPC, stable), auth.js (Bearer + sessions, stable), tools/ (one file per area + index.js registry: new tool = new file + one line), server.js (Express mount).

docs.title: A.3. Scope rules (apply to every tool)
docs.text:
1. Every call requires guildId, which must match the token's server (logical 403 otherwise) — shared helper src/mcp/tools/scope.js.
  2. Status comes from the roster: module_status and guild_info include the server's presence entry (name, members, snapshot freshness) read from the shared DB. If the bot is no (longer) in the server, the tool reports it (botPresente: false) but still answers — the roster is informative, never a blocker.
  3. Top limits are capped (default 10, max 25).

docs.title: A.4. Read tools (never writes)
docs.text: Tool What it does modules_list modules, versions, commands module_status on/off, 🛡️ protection, errors (per server) module_toggle turns a module on/off module_reset clears errors and protection (recovery) guild_snapshot modules + tickets + level top brain_search searches server skills/memories/files ticket_stats by type, avg close time, rating, staff top tickets_open open tickets with priority and claim brain_note_save / brain_note_forget writes/deletes server memories settings_get / settings_set AI provider, limits, logs (never API keys) economy_top, levels_top leaderboards user_cases / mod_history user moderation history bot_health uptime, mode, backend (honest nulls without client) config_get, shop_list, invites_top, channels_list, roles_list, analytics_summary, guild_info extra reads module_reload, module_config, announce_send writes via Commander economy_top wallet top (limit) levels_top level/XP top (limit) mod_history user moderation history (userId, limit) analytics_summary messages/joins/leaves for the last N days (days, max 30) config_get read-only server config (language, channels, automod…) shop_list roles-for-sale catalog invites_top top inviters (limit) channels_list live channels from Discord (id, name, type) roles_list live roles from Discord (id, name, color)

docs.title: A.5. Write tools (via Commander + scope, never direct DB)
docs.text:
Tool What it does Gate module_toggle turns a module on/off Commander.setModuleEnabled module_reload reloads without restart, clears errors+breaker Commander.reloadModule module_reset clears errors+protection Commander.resetModule module_config changes config (general, welcome, logging, levels, automod, autorole, starboard, confessioni, tickets, tempvoice, ai). Read first with config_get. Max 20-key patch, 2KB max values Commander.updateModuleConfig announce_send sends a message to a server text channel (verified in the live list, max 2000 chars, @everyone/@here neutralized) REST Bot token + channel scope

Example (Claude): "read config_get, raise the automod level with module_config, confirm with module_status, announce in #annunci with announce_send".

docs.title: A.6. Management
docs.text:
• /token lista — usage and last-use of every token
  • /token revoca id:... — disconnects Claude immediately

Security: tokens stored as sha256 only, never in logs; instant revocation; every write goes through the Commander gate like everything else.

docs.title: B. Client — connect the bot to AIs (Hermes style)
docs.text:
The bot becomes an MCP host: it connects to external servers (filesystem, github, fetch, sqlite, OpenAI-compatible gateway, local Ollama) and exposes them as mcp_<server>_<tool> tools, usable from Discord (/mcp chiama) and by the AI.

cp mcp/servers.example.json mcp/servers.json  # NEVER commit servers.json (tokens!)
# enable a server in servers.json, then from Discord:
/mcp stato     # connected / failed servers / registered tools
/mcp lista     # names like mcp_<server>_<tool>
/mcp chiama nome:mcp_fetch_fetch argomenti:{"url":"https://..."}
/mcp ricarica  # re-reads servers.json without restart

Format details, catalog (mcp/catalog.json) and stdio security: see mcp/README.md. Code: src/mcp/client/ — config.js (mcp_servers loader + ${VAR}), transports.js (stdio + Streamable HTTP, TAG sanitization), manager.js (4-wave discovery, include/exclude filters with globs, include wins, resources/prompts wrappers only if supported), aiBridge.js (function-specs for the AI), index.js (lazy singleton).

Env: MCP_ENABLED=1, MCP_SERVERS_PATH=./mcp/servers.json, MCP_TIMEOUT=30000. The native AI stays in src/ai/aiProviders.js (OPENAI_API_KEY keys etc., free Pollinations fallback): MCP adds tools, it doesn't replace providers.

docs.title: Agenti — JARVIS + specialisti (ZealBot)
docs.text: /jarvis affida compiti in linguaggio naturale. JARVIS (orchestratore) capisce, smista allo specialista giusto e resta responsabile del risultato. Gli specialisti non si chiamano tra loro: solo JARVIS → specialista (stesso principio del Commander: cervello → muscoli).

docs.title: Gli agenti
docs.text:
Agente Ruolo Esempi di compiti ⚡ JARVIS Orchestratore + generalista qualsiasi cosa; smista se serve 🛡️ Sentinel Moderazione e sicurezza piano anti-raid, soglie automod, procedure ban 🎫 Steward Ticket e supporto risposte pronte, moduli di accoglienza 🎵 Maestro Musica e vocali code, setup comandi musicali 💰 Banker Economia e livelli bilanci, premi, configurazioni XP 📚 Lore Conoscenza e codice riassunti, spiegazioni, memoria server 🔭 Scout Web e servizi esterni leggere pagine, usare servizi loggati

Uso: /jarvis compito:<testo> (JARVIS sceglie) oppure /jarvis compito:<testo> agente:scout (forzato). Il routing senza AI è a parole chiave e funziona sempre; con una chiave AI (anche gratis via default, vedi .env.example) gli specialisti ragionano a passi (ReAct, max JARVIS_MAX_STEPS).

docs.title: Sandbox per-agente
docs.text:
Ogni esecuzione gira in sandbox applicativa (src/agents/sandbox.js):

  • capability-based: solo i tool del manifest (say, note, fetchUrl, useService, askOwner) — niente require/fs/rete liberi;
  • jail directory: data/sandboxes/<agente>/ (gitignored);
  • timeout: JARVIS_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS (default 2 min);
  • audit: start/fine/errori nel logger, mai segreti nei log.

È isolamento logico, non una VM: protegge da errori e abusi via tool, non da codice nativo ostile (i plugin restano isolati dal pluginLoader).

docs.title: Goggles — la control-room (/agents.html)
docs.text:
Gli agenti non hanno uno schermo da condividere davvero: i goggles sono la traccia live di ogni sessione (pensieri → azioni → osservazioni → risultato), visibile in diretta su dashboard e alimentata dallo store condiviso (bot e dashboard sono processi separati).

Dalla control-room puoi:

  • 👁️ entrare nello schermo: apri una sessione e vedi lo stream live (SSE);
  • 🎧 take-over: dettare un'istruzione letta al passo successivo;
  • ✅/⛔ approvare o negare le richieste in attesa;
  • 🔑 vedere quali servizi hanno credenziali nel vault (mai i valori).

Su Discord, le approvazioni arrivano anche come bottoni (Approva/Nega) nel canale dove hai lanciato /jarvis.

docs.title: Vault — login ai servizi
docs.text:
Il proprietario salva credenziali (token/API key) e gli agenti usano i servizi senza mai vedere i segreti:

  1. imposta VAULT_KEY nel .env (min 16 caratteri, mai committarla);
  2. salva la credenziale (via codice: vault.storeSecret(servizio, account, segreto));
  3. lo specialista (oggi solo Scout) chiama useService: parte una richiesta di approvazione (dashboard + Discord);
  4. approvato → il broker inietta Authorization: Bearer <segreto> in una chiamata https e restituisce solo l'esito (il segreto viene oscurato se ricompare nell'output).

Limiti onesti: solo Bearer su https, niente host interni; niente bypass di captcha/2FA/login interattivi — per quelli serve l'umano. Ogni uso è tracciato (servizio, account, agente, sessione).

docs.title: API interne — Commander, Guardian, moduli
docs.text: Come pilotare il bot dal codice (comandi, dashboard, MCP, CLI passano tutti di qui). English edition: API.md.

docs.title: Commander (src/modules/commander.js + core packages/commander)
docs.text:
Orchestratore unico. Mai require diretto di modules/registry (lo smoke [8/5] lo vieta).

Metodo Firma Cosa fa checkGate(commandName, guildId) (string, string?) {ok:true} oppure {ok:false, reason:'disabled'\|'isolated', featureId}. Prima risolve comando → feature. canRun(guildId, featureId) (string?, string?) Stesso gate per feature id (per eventi/handler). Fail-open. executeCommand(command, interaction, client, opts?) opts.timeoutMs (default 15000) Esegue command.execute isolato con timeout; registra errori (breaker). Non lancia mai: {ok, timedOut?, error?}. guardEvent(file, event, args, client) — Avvolge ogni listener: salta se il modulo non può girare, registra errori. Non lancia mai. featureOfCommand/Event/Component (string) nome → feature id (oppure null = sempre consentito). listModules() — Descrittori statici (id, versione, comandi…). moduleHealth(guildId) — Stato per guild: enabled, isolated, errori, stats. setModuleEnabled(guildId, id, on) — Toggle (riattivare azzera anche breaker+errori). Lancia su id sconosciuto. reloadModule(guildId, id) — Rivalida la sintassi, ricarica il descrittore, azzera errori+breaker. resetModule(guildId, id) — Azzera errori+breaker. updateModuleConfig(guildId, mod, patch) — Instrada una patch validata al DB del modulo giusto. Lancia {status, message}. alertsPending() — Segnali dolore in coda (Guardian). guardianSummary(guildId) — Punteggi salute dal core TS (vedi sotto).

docs.title: Guardian (sistema immunitario)
docs.text:
• Score (passivo): core TS packages/commander (Guardian.observe/summary): ok/fail/timeout per guild+feature → {features, critical, weak, ok}. Niente LLM nell'hot path.
  • Dolore (attivo): registry.recordError ritorna {tripped}; al trip un segnale deduplicato va in coda (drainAlerts, finestra 15 min). src/jobs/guardianJob.js recapita nel canale log della guild ogni 2 min; ≥3 moduli isolati = febbre (1/ora).
  • Pelle: src/events/secretGuard.js cancella token/chiavi leakati + DM + modlog.
  • Salute quando vuoi: commander.guardianSummary(gid), commander.alertsPending().

docs.title: Configurazione per guild
docs.text:
Due strati (gli stessi di /config e dashboard):

  1. Toggle moduli — commander.setModuleEnabled(gid, id, on) (persistente via moduleState).
  2. Impostazioni moduli — commander.updateModuleConfig(gid, mod, patch) per general, welcome, logging, levels, automod, autorole, starboard, confessioni, tickets, tempvoice, ai (validati a monte; vedi MODULE_FIELDS in dashboard).
  3. Override env runtime — database/settings.js (setOverride/getOverride/effectiveEnv, whitelist rigida). Leggi via effectiveEnv(), mai process.env diretto per le chiavi modificabili.

docs.title: Estendere con un nuovo modulo
docs.text:
1. Descrittore src/modules/<id>.js via defineModule({id, title, commands, version…}) (validato, semver obbligatorio).
  2. Slash command in src/commands/<area>/ (autoload ricorsivo).
  3. Listener in src/events/ (un file per listener; eventi Discord condivisi sono pattern consentito, mai bypassare il gate — usa commander.canRun).
  4. Stato in src/database/<nome>.js sopra jsonDb (migrazioni additive in schema.js con timbro __v).
  5. Registra il feature id nelle mappe commander.featureOf* solo via descrittore (niente liste hardcoded altrove).
  6. Docs: il comando appare in docs/COMMANDS.md via node scripts/gen-docs.js; aggiungi una sezione smoke con chiavi qatest + cleanup.

docs.title: Decisione dashboard (bloccata)
docs.text: Opzione B: Express (src/dashboard) è l'unica dashboard supportata. L'app Next.js sperimentale è stata rimossa; non reintrodurre una seconda dashboard senza un ADR.

docs.title: Architettura del bot
docs.text: Mappa ricavata leggendo il codice (entry point src/index.js, eventi, database, dashboard, job). Nomi di file e comportamenti corrispondono a quanto implementato, non a intenzioni future.

docs.title: Panoramica
docs.text: ZealBot — bot Discord multi-server basato su discord.js v14, CommonJS, singolo processo Node (node src/index.js). Comandi slash organizzati per categoria-cartella, stato persistente in JSON (con backend SQLite opzionale), dashboard web in processo separato, job periodici avviati all'evento ready. Dettaglio variabili in CONFIG.md, comandi in COMMANDS.md (generato con node scripts/gen-docs.js).

docs.title: Struttura cartelle
docs.text: Percorso Ruolo src/index.js Entry point: client, caricamento comandi/eventi, login, avvio dashboard condizionale src/commands/<categoria>/*.js Comandi slash (data + execute + cooldown); la categoria è il nome cartella (ai, economy, fun, levels, moderation, music, tickets, utility) src/events/*.js Un file per listener (name + execute + once?); vedi pattern multi-listener sotto src/handlers/ ticketHandler.js, reactionRoleHandler.js: gestiscono select/modali/bottoni prima dei comandi src/database/ store.js + jsonDb.js (infrastruttura) + ~25 moduli di dominio (economy.js, levels.js, …) + rispettivi <nome>.json + moduleState.js (on/off feature per guild) src/modules/ Controller feature: registry.js + un file per parte (tickets.js, levels.js, … con comandi/db/eventi mappati); gate comandi/eventi, toggle dashboard, health ed errori isolati per modulo src/dashboard/ index.js (processo standalone), server.js, auth.js, api.js, guilds.js (source client/REST), presence.js (roster), discordRest.js (letture REST), public/: web app Express separata dal bot src/jobs/ ticketAutoclose.js, backup.js, selfImprove.js: timer avviati da events/ready.js, mai avviati altrove src/utils/ logger.js, i18n.js, ai.js/aiProviders.js, player.js, codebase.js, helpers.js, transcript.js, … src/locales/ it.js, en.js per utils/i18n.js scripts/smoke-test.js QA (npm test): comandi, eventi, roundtrip DB su chiavi qatest, require-safe scripts/gen-docs.js Genera docs/COMMANDS.md senza rete né bot deploy-commands.js Registra gli slash command su Discord (guild di test o globale)

docs.title: Avvio (src/index.js)
docs.text:
1. dotenv, require di DISCORD_TOKEN (exit 1 se manca).
  2. Client con 8 intent (Guilds, GuildMessages, MessageContent, GuildMembers, GuildModeration, GuildMessageReactions, GuildVoiceStates, GuildInvites) e partials (Message, Channel, GuildMember, Reaction).
  3. client.commands / client.cooldowns (Collection), client.spamMap (Map anti-spam in memoria).
  4. loadCommands(src/commands) ricorsiva: assegna command.category = <nome cartella>, ignora file senza data/execute con warning, segnala nomi slash duplicati senza sovrascrivere silenziosamente (l'ultimo vince nel Collection, con console.warn). Un require fallito salta solo quel file, mai tutto il bot.
  5. Registrazione eventi: un client.on/client.once per file, con validazione (name stringa + execute funzione); file non validi saltati con warning.
  6. Handler unhandledRejection/uncaughtException: log console + logger strutturato, mai crash.
  7. client.login(DISCORD_TOKEN); il bot scrive anche il roster guild (presence) per la dashboard standalone. Mai logica dashboard qui.

docs.title: Flusso interaction → comando (src/events/interactionCreate.js)
docs.text:
Ordine esatto della pipeline per ogni InteractionCreate:

  1. ticketHandler.handle(interaction) — se consuma (select, modali, bottoni ticket), stop.
  2. reactionRoleHandler.handle(interaction) — se consuma (select rr_select), stop. Entrambi con reply effimera di errore dedicata.
  3. Bottoni nuke_* — nuke_cancel annulla; nuke_confirm richiede permesso ManageChannels, clona il canale, elimina l'originale e conferma (reply via webhook perché il canale originale non esiste più).
  4. Solo isChatInputCommand() prosegue; comando cercato in client.commands per interaction.commandName.
  5. Gate controller (src/modules/registry): se la feature del comando è spenta per la guild, stop con reply effimera (DM sempre consentite). Gli errori di execute vengono registrati per feature (dashboard).
  6. Permessi custom (database/customPerms, stile PeakBot) — ruoli per-comando per guild, con bypass Administrator. Sta prima del cooldown di proposito: chi viene respinto non consuma attesa.
  7. Cooldown per comando+utente (command.cooldown || 3 secondi), con messaggio effimero di attesa in formato timestamp relativo.
  8. command.execute(interaction, client) + logCommand(...) per le analytics. In caso di errore: log strutturato, embed best-effort nel logChannelId della guild (database/guildConfig), rimborso del cooldown (timestamps.delete) così un errore non fa pagare attesa, reply effimera generica.

docs.title: Pattern multi-listener (eventi)
docs.text:
index.js registra un listener per file, quindi più file sullo stesso evento Discord sono più listener attivi — è un pattern voluto solo per questi eventi (verificato dallo smoke test, corpi disgiunti):

  • guildMemberAdd — welcome (guildMemberAdd.js), autorole (autorole.js), anti-raid (antiRaid.js), analytics joins (analyticsMembers.js), inviti (inviteTracker.js).
  • messageCreate — XP/automod (messageCreate.js), autoresponder (autoResponder.js, solo lettura + reply), conteggio analytics (analyticsMessages.js).
  • voiceStateUpdate — stanze vocali temporanee (tempVoice.js), XP vocale (voiceXp.js).

Qualsiasi altro evento duplicato su due file è un errore (lo smoke test fallisce). Altri listener singoli notevoli: aiMention.js, aiModeration.js, auditLog.js, customCommands.js, starboard.js, snipe via utils/snipeCache.js, ready.js.

docs.title: Persistenza (src/database/store.js + jsonDb.js)
docs.text:
• store.js — API sincrona collection(nome) con get/set/update/delete/all. Backend da env a ogni operazione (i test cambiano env a runtime):
  • DB_BACKEND=json (default): file src/database/<nome>.json, read-modify-write atomico via tmp+rename; file corrotti copiati in <file>.corrupt-<timestamp> invece di perderli.
  • DB_BACKEND=sqlite: node:sqlite su DB_SQLITE_PATH (default ./data/bot.db), tabella kv(collection, key, value) con valori JSON, journal_mode=WAL, transazioni su replace multi-riga; se il driver manca o l'apertura fallisce, fallback a json con warning (mai crash, mai perdita dati).
  • Postgres futuro, non attivo: solo schema in src/database/postgres-schema.sql; richiederebbe API async separata.
  • jsonDb.js — compat layer load/save/dbFile sopra store.js, così i ~25 moduli di dominio (economy, levels, warnings, guildConfig, tickets, cases, shop, lotteria, rep, sfide, confessioni, reactionRoles, autoresponder, invites, tempvoice, stanze, levelRewards, analytics, customPerms, customCommands, aiConfig, starboard, …) funzionano invariati su entrambi i backend.

docs.title: Dashboard processo separato (src/dashboard/)
docs.text:
• Avviata con npm run dashboard (src/dashboard/index.js, richiede DASHBOARD_PORT); express è required lazy dentro startDashboard() così lo smoke test passa anche senza express installato.
  • Legge lo stesso store DB del bot (nessuna sincronizzazione) + roster presence scritto dal bot; dettagli Discord live via REST con Bot token.
  • server.js: JSON limit 256kb, static public/, route auth, /api protetta da auth.requireAuth, landing con fallback inline se public/index.html manca, 404 JSON, error handler che non crasha mai.
  • auth.js: OAuth2 Discord (redirect <BASE_URL>/callback, scope identify+guilds) con SESSION_SECRET, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, BASE_URL.
  • api.js: API per-guild riservate agli admin dei server in comune.

docs.title: Job (src/jobs/, avviati da src/events/ready.js)
docs.text:
Job Schedulazione Cosa fa ticketAutoclose ogni 15 min Chiude ticket inattivi oltre autoCloseDays (setAutoClose, 0 = off, max 90) backup ogni notte ore 03:00 locali Copia src/database/*.json (+ sqlite se esiste) in backups/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm/, retention 7 giorni, journal backups/last.json; mai crashare selfImprove notturno SELF_IMPROVE_TIME Attivo solo con SELF_IMPROVE=1 (default off); rilegge il codice e propone una patch, mai commit automatici, SELF_IMPROVE_DRY_RUN=1 per solo report

Tutti usano interval con unref così non tengono vivo il processo da soli, e ogni avvio è wrappato in try/catch in ready.js.

docs.title: Deploy comandi e i18n
docs.text:
• deploy-commands.js — scansiona src/commands (un livello), pusha data.toJSON() via REST: su guild di test se GUILD_ID impostato, altrimenti globale (fino a ~1h di propagazione).
  • utils/i18n.js + locales/it.js/en.js — testi di risposta localizzati per guild (getLang/t); nomi e descrizioni slash restano in italiano.
  • Musica (utils/player.js, comando /musica) — discord-player con extractor; errori di dipendenze vocali mappati in messaggi italiani, mai crash.

docs.title: Configurazione (variabili d'ambiente)
docs.text:
Tutte le env lette dal codice (grep process.env in src/, deploy-commands.js) più .env.example. Copia .env.example in .env e compila almeno le obbligatorie. Mai committare .env.

La configurazione per-server (lingua, canali, welcome, automod, ticket, livelli, AI, permessi) avviene esclusivamente dalla dashboard web (<BASE_URL>/app.html, sezioni Generale, Moderazione, Livelli, Ticket e Vocali, AI ed Extra, Permessi). Questo file descrive solo le variabili d'ambiente del processo.

Variabile Obbligatoria Default Dove usata Note DISCORD_TOKEN sì — src/index.js, deploy-commands.js Token del bot. Senza, il bot esce con errore. CLIENT_ID sì (per deploy comandi e dashboard) — deploy-commands.js, src/dashboard/auth.js Application ID. deploy-commands.js lo usa senza fallback. GUILD_ID no — (deploy globale) deploy-commands.js Se impostato, registra i comandi solo sul server di test (veloce); altrimenti globale (fino a ~1h). AI_PROVIDER no auto src/utils/aiProviders.js auto sceglie da solo tra le chiavi presenti; valori: openai, anthropic, gemini, groq, openrouter, mistral, deepseek, xai, together, cerebras, ollama, fireworks, novita, huggingface, nvidia, kimi, pollinations (+ alias claude, google, grok, hf); valore ignoto + AI_API_URL = endpoint OpenAI-compatibile custom. OPENAI_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default gpt-4o-mini. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default claude-3-5-haiku-20241022. GEMINI_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default gemini-2.0-flash. GROQ_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default llama-3.3-70b-versatile. OPENROUTER_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default openai/gpt-4o-mini. MISTRAL_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default mistral-small-latest. DEEPSEEK_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default deepseek-chat. XAI_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default grok-3-mini. TOGETHER_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo. CEREBRAS_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default llama3.1-8b (velocissimo). Chiavi multiple con virgola = pool stile Hermes (sk-a,sk-b: rotazione + failover chiave). FIREWORKS_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p6. NOVITA_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 (200+ modelli via AI_MODEL). HF_TOKEN no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Hugging Face Inference Providers, default deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2. NVIDIA_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Modello default nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b. KIMI_API_KEY no (ne basta una) — src/utils/aiProviders.js Moonshot, default kimi-for-coding. AI_MODEL no modello default del provider src/utils/aiProviders.js Accetta provider:modello stile Hermes (es. groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile, vince su AI_PROVIDER). Override endpoint via <PREFIX>_BASE_URL (es. GROQ_BASE_URL). AI_FALLBACKS no — (nessun failover) src/utils/aiProviders.js Es. groq,openrouter: se il primario fallisce (rate, timeout, rete, HTTP, chiave), prova in ordine. Se falliscono tutti, l'errore mostrato è del primario. OLLAMA_HOST no http://localhost:11434 src/utils/aiProviders.js Con AI_PROVIDER=ollama: IA locale (default llama3.1), zero cloud, nessuna chiave. AI_API_URL no https://text.pollinations.ai src/utils/aiProviders.js Endpoint OpenAI-compatibile custom; senza chiavi si usa Pollinations gratis, nessuna chiave richiesta. AI_API_KEY no — src/utils/aiProviders.js Chiave per AI_API_URL custom. AI_DAILY_LIMIT no 500 src/utils/ai.js Budget giornaliero chiamate AI su chiave condivisa (0 = illimitato). Oltre il limite l'AI risponde "Budget giornaliero esaurito". DB_BACKEND no json src/database/store.js json (file src/database/*.json) o sqlite (tabella kv via node:sqlite, Node 22+). Valori diversi da sqlite ricadono su json. DB_SQLITE_PATH no ./data/bot.db src/database/store.js, src/jobs/backup.js Path del database sqlite (directory creata se manca, journal_mode=WAL). Incluso nel backup se il file esiste. Se node:sqlite manca: fallback a json con warning. LOG_LEVEL no info src/utils/logger.js debug, info, warn, error. Log JSON-lines su console + logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log. LOG_DIR no logs src/utils/logger.js Directory dei file di log giornalieri. BACKUP_DIR no backups src/jobs/backup.js Destinazione backup notturni YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm/, retention 7 giorni, journal last.json. Non presente in .env.example (trovata via grep). SELF_IMPROVE no off src/jobs/selfImprove.js Solo =1 attiva il self-improvement notturno. Mai commit automatici: revisiona con git diff. SELF_IMPROVE_TIME no 22:00 src/jobs/selfImprove.js Ora locale di esecuzione. SELF_IMPROVE_DRY_RUN no off src/jobs/selfImprove.js =1: solo report, nessuna patch applicata. SELF_IMPROVE_GUILD_ID no — (solo log) src/jobs/selfImprove.js Server dove inviare il report notturno. DASHBOARD_PORT no — (dashboard spenta) src/dashboard/index.js Richiesta da npm run dashboard (processo separato); senza, la dashboard non parte. SESSION_SECRET sì (se dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js Segreto sessione, almeno 32 caratteri casuali. CLIENT_SECRET sì (se dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js Client secret dell'app Discord (OAuth2). BASE_URL sì (se dashboard) — src/dashboard/auth.js, comando /help URL pubblico (es. http://localhost:3000); deve combaciare col redirect OAuth2 <BASE_URL>/callback. Usato anche nel footer di /help.

Note:

  • Le chiavi AI sono alternative: basta una chiave e il provider è scelto in automatico (AI_PROVIDER=auto); senza chiavi funziona gratis via Pollinations (AI_API_URL default).
  • Timeout AI fisso 25 s nel codice (src/utils/aiProviders.js), non configurabile via env.
  • Backup sempre ore 03:00 locali e retention 7 giorni: costanti nel codice (src/jobs/backup.js), non env.

docs.text:
I testi di risposta passano da src/core/i18n.js (motore i18next con fs-backend sopra src/locales/<lingua>.json, fallback inline se il backend fallisce): t(guildId, chiave, vars) con fallback per-chiave all'inglese, getGuildLanguage(guildId) legge language da guildConfig (si cambia con /language, solo admin; /lingua rimanda alla dashboard). Lingue supportate: en, it (fallback en). src/utils/i18n.js mantiene la vecchia API t(chiave, lingua, vars) sugli stessi JSON per i chiamanti esistenti.

Copertura attuale: comandi moderazione, economy, ticket, livelli; nomi e descrizioni slash restano in italiano.

Per aggiungere una lingua (es. es):

  1. Copia src/locales/en.json in src/locales/es.json e traduci i valori (le chiavi mancanti ricadono sull'inglese automaticamente).
  2. Aggiungi 'es' a SUPPORTED in src/core/i18n.js (e a SUPPORTED_LANGS in src/utils/i18n.js per i chiamanti legacy).
  3. Usa t(guildId, 'chiave', { vars }) nei nuovi testi invece di stringhe hardcoded; non cambiare i testi esistenti senza motivo.

docs.title: Hosting — ZealBot
docs.text:
Guida in italiano per avviare il bot ovunque. Via rapida per tutti:

npm run setup   # rileva l'host, verifica il token live, scrive .env
npm run deploy  # registra gli slash command
npm start       # bot (+ dashboard con npm run dashboard)

Requisiti comuni:

  • Node.js ≥ 22.12 (consigliato Node 24; @discordjs/voice lo richiede)
  • Toolchain: npm per tutto (bot + dashboard Express).
  • File .env creato da .env.example con almeno DISCORD_TOKEN e CLIENT_ID
  • Deploy degli slash command: npm run deploy (dopo ogni aggiunta/modifica di comandi)
  • Start: npm start (= node src/index.js) · Test: npm test

docs.title: Matrice host (rilevata in automatico da src/host/)
docs.text:
Host Disco Storage consigliato Dashboard Note Render effimero sqlite su Disk (/app/data) ✅ via $PORT Blueprint render.yaml Railway effimero sqlite su Volume ✅ via $PORT railway.toml (Dockerfile root) Fly.io effimero sqlite su Volume (/app/data) ✅ porta 3000 fly.toml (healthcheck /healthz: imposta le env dashboard) Pterodactyl persistente sqlite ✅ porta pannello Egg NodeJS generico Docker effimero* sqlite su volume ✅ $PORT/3000 docker-compose.yml (*persistente con volume) VPS / locale persistente sqlite (Node 22+) o json ✅ PM2 consigliato Termux persistente json ✅ Sviluppo, non produzione Replit persistente json ✅ Sempre-on a pagamento

Persistenza dati: di default il bot usa JSON in src/database/*.json (DB_BACKEND=json). Per hosting con filesystem effimero (Railway/Render/Docker) usa invece SQLite: DB_BACKEND=sqlite + DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db (richiede Node ≥ 22, usa node:sqlite, zero dipendenze extra), con la cartella data/ su volume/disco persistente.

docs.title: 1. Termux (Android)
docs.text:
pkg update && pkg install -y nodejs git
git clone <repo> zealbot && cd zealbot
npm ci
cp .env.example .env   # poi compila con il tuo editor
npm run deploy
npm start

Note Termux:

  • Niente systemd: per tenerlo attivo usa termux-wake-lock + sessione tmux, oppure PM2 (npm i -g pm2 && pm2 start ecosystem.config.js && pm2 save). PM2 non riparte da solo al riavvio del telefono: riapri Termux e fai pm2 resurrect.
  • Su Termux resta su DB_BACKEND=json (default) a meno di avere Node ≥ 22.
  • I log vanno in logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log (LOG_LEVEL=info di default).

docs.title: 2. VPS (Debian/Ubuntu) — systemd oppure PM2
docs.text:
# Node 24 LTS (nodesource) + clone
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_24.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt install -y nodejs git
git clone <repo> /opt/zealbot && cd /opt/zealbot
npm ci --omit=dev
cp .env.example .env   # compila DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, ...
npm run deploy

docs.title: Opzione A: systemd (consigliato)
docs.text:
sudo cp zealbot.service /etc/systemd/system/zealbot.service
# adatta User/percorsi nel file se non usi utente "bot" o /opt/zealbot
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now zealbot
systemctl status zealbot
journalctl -u zealbot -f   # log live

Il file zealbot.service usa WorkingDirectory=/opt/zealbot, EnvironmentFile=/opt/zealbot/.env e Restart=always.

docs.title: Opzione B: PM2
docs.text:
sudo npm i -g pm2
pm2 start ecosystem.config.js   # fork, 1 istanza, log in logs/pm2-*.log
pm2 save && pm2 startup         # riavvio automatico al boot
pm2 logs zealbot

Una sola istanza mi raccomando (fork, mai cluster): il bot usa DB su file, due istanze scriverebbero gli stessi JSON/SQLite e corromperebbero i dati.

docs.title: 3. Docker
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env   # compila i valori
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose logs -f

# Con dashboard web (profilo opzionale, richiede DASHBOARD_* nel .env):
docker compose --profile dashboard up -d --build
  • Dockerfile: base node:24-slim, npm ci --omit=dev, utente non-root node, NODE_ENV=production, volumi /app/data /app/logs /app/backups.
  • docker-compose.yml: servizio bot (restart: unless-stopped, env_file: .env, volumi ./data ./logs ./backups); servizio bot-dashboard (solo profilo dashboard) con porta ${DASHBOARD_PORT:-3000} pubblicata.
  • Healthcheck condizionale (vedi commento nel Dockerfile): senza DASHBOARD_PORT il bot non espone HTTP, quindi l'healthcheck ritorna subito sano (i crash li copre restart: unless-stopped); con dashboard attiva fa GET /healthz (endpoint pubblico con fallback a /) via node -e ... fetch(...) senza bisogno di curl nell'immagine.
  • In container imposta DB_BACKEND=sqlite + DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db (il compose lo fa già di default): i JSON di src/database/ non sono montati come volume perché convivono con i moduli .js (montare la cartella nasconderebbe il codice al container).
  • Musica: l'immagine node:24-slim non include ffmpeg (serve a discord-player/@discordjs/voice). Se usi i comandi musicali, aggiungi nel Dockerfile prima di USER node: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*.

docs.title: Immagine precompilata (GHCR, senza build)
docs.text:
Ogni tag vX.Y.Z pubblica ghcr.io/zema-tech/zealbot-discord:latest (multi-arch amd64/arm64) via .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:

services:
  bot:
    image: ghcr.io/zema-tech/zealbot-discord:latest
    env_file: .env
    environment:
      DB_BACKEND: sqlite
      DB_SQLITE_PATH: /app/data/bot.db
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

docs.title: 4. Railway / Render
docs.text:
Via rapida (Render): il repo include render.yaml (Docker + healthcheck /healthz + disco da 1GB): New → Blueprint, poi compila le env segrete (DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET, BASE_URL). Il blueprint punta già SQLite su disco (DB_SQLITE_PATH=/app/data/bot.db).

Procedura manuale (valida per entrambi, filesystem effimero: serve disco persistente):

  1. Crea il servizio dal repo (Build: npm ci, Start: node src/index.js).
  2. Imposta le Environment Variables dal pannello (copia le chiavi di .env.example): DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID, DB_BACKEND=sqlite, DB_SQLITE_PATH=./data/bot.db, ed eventualmente DASHBOARD_* (su Render apri anche la porta con DASHBOARD_PORT).
  3. Monta un disco persistente sul percorso data/ (es. Railway Volume → mount /app/data; Render Disk su runtime Docker → mount /app/data, su runtime Node nativo → /opt/render/project/src/data): lì vivono bot.db, logs/ e backups/. Senza disco, a ogni deploy riparti da zero (economia, livelli, ticket… persi).
  4. Esegui npm run deploy una volta (da locale con le stesse env, oppure come one-off job): registra gli slash command su Discord.
  5. Render free: lo spin-down per inattività spegne il bot (il bot deve stare sempre online) — serve istanza sempre attiva o un piano a pagamento.

docs.title: 5. Pterodactyl — nota egg
docs.text:
Nessun egg ufficiale: usa un egg generico NodeJS (versione 20):

  • Startup Command: node src/index.js
  • Install Script: npm ci (o npm ci --omit=dev)
  • Environment / Variables: DISCORD_TOKEN, CLIENT_ID (+ DB_BACKEND, AI_*, DASHBOARD_* se servono) — oppure monta/carica un file .env nella root del server.
  • I dati restano sul disco del server Pterodactyl (persistenti tra i riavvii); fai backup regolari di src/database/*.json (o di data/bot.db se usi SQLite) con il comando /backup o dal pannello.
  • Il deploy comandi (node deploy-commands.js) va lanciato una volta da console dopo aver impostato le variabili.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Sintomo Causa probabile e fix Unsupported URL Type "workspace:" su npm install Resto storico: aggiorna il lock con npm install e riprova (i workspace orfani sono stati rimossi). DisallowedIntents / bot online ma non risponde Abilita nel Developer Portal → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents: Server Members Intent e Message Content Intent (il bot usa GuildMembers + MessageContent, vedi src/index.js). GuildPresences non serve. Slash command mancanti o vecchi Lancia npm run deploy (serve CLIENT_ID; con GUILD_ID i comandi arrivano subito sul server di test, senza devi attendere fino a ~1h per la propagazione globale). TokenInvalid / TOKEN_INVALID DISCORD_TOKEN errato o rigenerato: aggiorna .env (mai committarlo) e riavvia. Bot non ha effetto (ruoli, timeout, canali) Permessi: invita il bot con scope bot + applications.commands e permessi adeguati (Gestire ruoli/canali, Bannare, Moderare membri per i timeout, Connettersi/Parlare per la musica). Il ruolo del bot deve stare sopra i ruoli che deve gestire, altrimenti Discord rifiuta in silenzio. Dashboard: redirect OAuth fallito BASE_URL deve corrispondere al Redirect URI registrato nel portale Discord (<BASE_URL>/callback, scope identify+guilds); servono anche CLIENT_SECRET e SESSION_SECRET (≥32 caratteri). Porta occupata / dashboard non apre Cambia DASHBOARD_PORT nel .env; verifica che la porta sia esposta (firewall/VPS, ports: nel compose, porta aperta su Render). Musica che non parte / errori voice Servono ffmpeg e dipendenze libsodium/opus (su VPS: apt install ffmpeg; su Docker vedi §3). Senza, gli altri comandi funzionano comunque. DB azzerato dopo un redeploy Filesystem effimero senza volume: passa a DB_BACKEND=sqlite con data/ persistente (§4). In locale fai /backup regolari (finiscono in backups/). Crash loop / restart continui Leggi logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log (o journalctl/pm2 logs/docker compose logs): quasi sempre è .env incompleto (DISCORD_TOKEN mancante → exit 1 immediato).

docs.title: MCP — telecomando del bot (stile Hermes Agent)
docs.text:
Ispirato a NousResearch/hermes-agent: stessi concetti (mcp_servers, tools.include/exclude, stdio + Streamable HTTP, prefisso mcp_<server>_<tool>), adattati al bot.

Direzione Cosa fa Config A. Server (IA → bot) Claude/ChatGPT operano il bot via POST /mcp /token crea, snippet in mcp/claude.example.json B. Client (bot → IA/tool) Il bot usa MCP server esterni come tool mcp/servers.json (da mcp/servers.example.json), comando /mcp

docs.title: A. Server — telecomando del bot
docs.text: Il bot espone un MCP server (Streamable HTTP) su POST /mcp. Protocollo (src/mcp/protocol.js) e auth Bearer (src/mcp/auth.js) sono stabili e non si toccano: ogni token vale per un solo server e ogni tool lo enforza.

docs.title: A.1. Crea il token (una volta, da Discord)
docs.text:
Essendo proprietario del server:

/token crea nome:claude-casa

Copia il token mostrato (non sarà più recuperabile) e l'endpoint:

https://TUO-HOST/mcp

docs.title: A.2. Collega Claude
docs.text:
Claude Code (consigliato):

claude mcp add --transport http zealbot https://TUO-HOST/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer dbt_..."

Claude Desktop: Impostazioni → Connettori → Aggiungi con URL + header Authorization: Bearer dbt_.... Lo stesso snippet è pronto in mcp/claude.example.json.

Altri client MCP: endpoint POST /mcp, protocollo 2025-06-18, metodi initialize (risponde con header Mcp-Session-Id, da rimandare), tools/list, tools/call. GET /mcp apre uno stream SSE (serve sessione), DELETE /mcp la chiude.

Struttura codice: src/mcp/ — protocol.js (JSON-RPC, stabile), auth.js (Bearer + sessioni, stabile), tools/ (un file per area + index.js registro: nuovo tool = nuovo file + una riga), server.js (mount Express).

docs.title: A.3. Regole di scope (valgono per tutti i tool)
docs.text:
1. Ogni chiamata richiede guildId, che deve matchare il server del token (403 logico altrimenti) — helper condiviso src/mcp/tools/scope.js.
  2. Lo status viene dal roster: module_status e guild_info includono la voce presence del server (nome, membri, freschezza snapshot) letta dal DB condiviso. Se il bot non è (più) nel server, il tool lo segnala (botPresente: false) ma risponde comunque — il roster è informativo, mai un blocco.
  3. I limit dei top sono cappati (default 10, max 25).

docs.title: A.4. Tool di lettura (mai scritture)
docs.text: Tool Cosa fa modules_list moduli, versioni, comandi module_status on/off, protezione 🛡️, errori (per server) module_toggle accende/spegne un modulo module_reset azzera errori e protezione (recupero) guild_snapshot moduli + ticket + top livelli brain_search cerca in skill/memorie/file del server ticket_stats per tipo, chiusura media, rating, top staff tickets_open ticket aperti con priorità e claim brain_note_save / brain_note_forget scrive/cancella memorie del server settings_get / settings_set provider IA, limiti, log (mai chiavi API) economy_top, levels_top classifiche user_cases / mod_history storico moderazione utente bot_health uptime, modalità, backend (null onesti senza client) config_get, shop_list, invites_top, channels_list, roles_list, analytics_summary, guild_info letture extra module_reload, module_config, announce_send scritture via Commander economy_top top portafogli (limit) levels_top top livelli/XP (limit) mod_history storico moderazione di un utente (userId, limit) analytics_summary messaggi/ingressi/uscite ultimi N giorni (days, max 30) config_get config server in sola lettura (lingua, canali, automod…) shop_list catalogo ruoli in vendita invites_top top invitanti (limit) channels_list canali live da Discord (id, nome, tipo) roles_list ruoli live da Discord (id, nome, colore)

docs.title: A.5. Tool di scrittura (via Commander + scope, mai DB diretti)
docs.text:
Tool Cosa fa Gate module_toggle accende/spegne un modulo Commander.setModuleEnabled module_reload ricarica senza restart, azzera errori+breaker Commander.reloadModule module_reset azzera errori+protezione Commander.resetModule module_config cambia config (general, welcome, logging, levels, automod, autorole, starboard, confessioni, tickets, tempvoice, ai). Leggi prima con config_get. Patch max 20 chiavi, valori max 2KB Commander.updateModuleConfig announce_send invia un messaggio in un canale testuale del server (verificato in lista live, max 2000 char, @everyone/@here neutralizzati) REST Bot token + scope canale

Esempio (Claude): "leggi config_get, alza il livello di automod con module_config, conferma con module_status, avvisa in #annunci con announce_send".

docs.title: A.6. Gestione
docs.text:
• /token lista — usi e ultimo uso di ogni token
  • /token revoca id:... — stacca Claude subito

Sicurezza: token salvati solo come sha256, mai nei log; revoca istantanea; ogni scrittura passa dal gate Commander come tutto il resto.

docs.title: B. Client — collega il bot alle IA (stile Hermes)
docs.text:
Il bot diventa host MCP: si collega a server esterni (filesystem, github, fetch, sqlite, gateway OpenAI-compatibile, Ollama locale) e li espone come tool mcp_<server>_<tool>, usabili da Discord (/mcp chiama) e dalla AI.

cp mcp/servers.example.json mcp/servers.json  # MAI committare servers.json (token!)
# abilita un server in servers.json, poi da Discord:
/mcp stato     # connessi / falliti / tool registrati
/mcp lista     # nomi mcp_<server>_<tool>
/mcp chiama nome:mcp_fetch_fetch argomenti:{"url":"https://..."}
/mcp ricarica  # rilegge servers.json senza riavviare

Dettagli formato, catalogo (mcp/catalog.json) e sicurezza stdio: vedi mcp/README.md. Codice: src/mcp/client/ — config.js (loader mcp_servers + ${VAR}), transports.js (stdio + Streamable HTTP, sanitizzazione TAG), manager.js (discovery a ondate da 4, filtri include/exclude con glob, include vince, wrapper resources/prompts solo se supportati), aiBridge.js (function-specs per la AI), index.js (singleton lazy).

Env: MCP_ENABLED=1, MCP_SERVERS_PATH=./mcp/servers.json, MCP_TIMEOUT=30000. La AI nativa resta in src/ai/aiProviders.js (chiavi OPENAI_API_KEY ecc., fallback gratis Pollinations): MCP aggiunge tool, non sostituisce i provider.
